parts.text: Which claim correctly explains what happens to the dead matter and waste?

options.text: Fungi, bacteria, and other microorganisms grow on the dead matter and break down the waste.
The dead matter vanishes on its own, and mushrooms are only umbrella shapes with no role in breakdown.
Only animals remove dead matter; microorganisms never act on waste in nature.
Microorganisms break down waste only after humans add chemicals to the log.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Adil finds mushrooms on a fallen log and notices soft waste under leaf litter disappearing over weeks.

part_answers.answer: Decomposer microorganisms such as fungi and bacteria grow on dead matter and waste and break them down in nature.

teacher.key_rationale: Fungi, bacteria, and other microorganisms decompose dead matter and waste. Claiming dead matter vanishes alone, denying microbial action, or requiring human chemicals all miss that hinge.
